_about: Shot structures: how an ad is filmed and cut, picked per video from what its script argues (ad-brief-compiler section 2). A video's format (templates/formats.json) is the argument; its structure is the camera and the edit. Each: what it is, which arguments it serves, the 8 scene rows (A01-B04, [size, move, what the row shows]; 'argued' has one map per format), the edit's pace, whether the punchline gets the 1.15 zoom and a Slide Blur ('transitions': [] for none; left out = the format's), whether the size must change at every cut (cut_sheet.py prints SAME SIZE), and the risk to write against. An explore group uses at least two structures across V1-V3; an iterate group keeps the control's unless structure is its variable.

argued.name: Argued cuts
argued.idea: each sentence its own shot size and camera move, the shot proving what the sentence says; the size changes at every cut
argued.fits: turn, myth, list, after: an argument with a problem, a turn and reasons to show
argued.pace: one or two shots a sentence, a hard cut to a new size on every sentence
argued.risk: close-ups of a sculptural product drift: keep where the part meets the rest in frame

follow.name: One-take follow
follow.idea: one continuous handheld moment: the camera follows ACTOR A through the room and arrives at the product; the size flows from wide to close as they reach it, and each row continues the last one's action and position
follow.fits: story, ritual: a lived moment, first person, the product as part of the day
follow.pace: few cuts: one at the punchline and where the two generated parts meet; each shot runs long
follow.risk: one long action gives the model time to drift people and the product: every row repeats ACTOR A's clothes and the product's outline and place
rows: ACTOR A walks into the room, the product ahead of them
still walking, the room's problem or moment in passing
their hand on the part the sentence names, body in frame
the same action carried on as they settle
ACTOR A at home with it, the room around

tableau.name: Still-life tableaux
tableau.idea: composed, near-still frames like a catalogue page in a lived room: the product centred, ACTOR A stepping into and out of frame, slow push-ins, the light doing the work
tableau.fits: gift, aspiration, a premium piece, an offer-led ad: the piece as something worth owning
tableau.pace: one slow shot a sentence, clean hard cuts, no zoom
tableau.risk: near-still frames make Negen copy the poster and barely move: every row names a slow push-in or a slow slide, and ACTOR A moves

the room composed around the product
the piece itself, centred, outline in frame
ACTOR A steps in and uses it

pov.name: First-person
pov.idea: the camera is ACTOR A's eyes at standing or sitting height: the viewer does what they do (sets the cup down, reaches for the book); their own hands come in from the bottom edge at waist or table height
pov.fits: ritual, list, story: use and convenience, what it is like to live with it
pov.pace: one or two shots a sentence, cuts on the hand actions
pov.risk: hands: only from the bottom edge to waist or table height (section 6); ACTOR A is seen whole only in a mirror-free WIDE or the end frame
rows: ACTOR A's view entering the room, the product ahead
the problem or moment in front of them, their hands at table height
their hand sets something on the product
the top and what sits on it, their hand reaching
they sit or step back: the product beside them

match.name: Before/after match cuts
match.idea: the same framing twice: the room without the product, then a hard cut to the identical frame with it; the change is the punchline
match.fits: after, turn, myth: a visible change to the room
match.pace: hold the before, a hard match cut on the turn, then the argued rows
match.risk: the model plays two framings in reverse or dissolves them (section 1): the before and the after are separate rows (A02, A03), the framing written in the same words in both
rows: hook: ACTOR A in the room
the before: the wall or corner without our product, framing named exactly
the after: the identical frame, our product in it (hard cut)
the part that made the difference
ACTOR A beside it for scale

montage.name: Detail montage
montage.idea: quick beats of 1-1.5 s on details and uses, a cut on every beat, building to the product whole
montage.fits: list: many reasons, comparing buyers; a product with several features to show
montage.pace: two or three shots a sentence, a hard cut on every beat
montage.risk: many close-ups mean more drift: every close row keeps the outline in frame, and the shot check is strict on them
rows: the promise: ACTOR A with the product
detail two: the top in use
detail three: its height or base
a hand using it, body in frame
ACTOR A in the room with it
